ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a series-type voltage regulation circuit, with an unregulated input Vi = 15 V marked at the upper left end, and an output Vo = 9 V marked at the upper right end. On the right side of the output terminal there is a sampling voltage-divider branch: R1 = 1 kΩ is connected from the Vo terminal to the middle sampling node, and R2 is connected from this sampling node to ground. This sampling node is connected through a horizontal connecting line to the relevant node of the error-amplifying transistor. At the lower left there is a Zener diode connected to ground, labeled Vz = 3.3 V. The problem statement explains that the base currents of the two BJTs can be ignored, and VBE = 0.7 V. Reasoning: According to the specified method, R1 and R2 form an unloaded voltage divider from Vo = 9 V to ground. The error transistor and Zener reference make the sampling node voltage Vz + VBE = 3.3 V + 0.7 V = 4.0 V. Since the base current can be ignored, the voltage-divider relationship is 4.0 = 9 * R2 / (1000 + R2). Solving gives: 4(1000 + R2) = 9R2, that is, 4000 + 4R2 = 9R2, so 5R2 = 4000, R2 = 800 Ω.
